newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES END MIXED, SPOTS UP.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI T-BILL REPO RATES END MIXED, SPOTS UP.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mixed on Tuesday with increased fund demand on a new domestic A share issue balanced by the poor performance of the A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 10.90 percent from 11.00 percent on Monday.
But the shortest three-day contract surged to 14.10 percent from 11.99 percent due to an issue of 90 million A shares by Jingzhou Shihua Co on the Shenzhen stock exchange on Tuesday, traders said.
Total turnover oN the six-contract market rose to 4.25 million lots from 3.29 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Traders said the new A share issue in Shenzhen boosted fund demand, in particular in the early-maturing contracts.
"The volume of the seven-day and three-day contracts rose sharply on Tuesday with institutions borrowing heavily for bidding for the newly-issued shares," one trader said.
But sharp falls on both the Shanghai and Shenzhen A share markets on Tuesday left many institutions reluctant to borrow on the repo market and prevented a solid rise in the rates.
Traders said they expected the repo rates to consolidate on Wednesday partly due to a lack of new A share issues.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly higher on Tuesday on a technical rebound after several days of consolidation, but trading was dull, indicating market sentiment was still weak, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in July 2006 rose to 100.19 yuan from 100.09 yuan. Volume on the eight-contract market fell to 530,565 lots from 581,624 lots.
Traders said they expected the spot contracts to move narrowly around current levels in the next few days.
